preamble: Monophthongization of the diphthong [ou] to the close back vowel [u]. In late Old French (c. 1250–1300) the diphthong /ou/, which had arisen from earlier /ol/, /ɔl/ and /aul/ before a consonant, became /u/ everywhere, giving pousse, chou, fou and coup.

examples.from: Old French pousse with /ou/ '(he) pushes' (< Latin pulsat)
Old French chou with /ou/ 'cabbage' (< Latin caulis)
Old French fou with /ou/ 'crazy' (< Latin follem)
Old French coup with /ou/ 'blow' (< Latin colaphum, *colpum)

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Phonological history of French. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_French
